messages:
alex: Quick question — we keep seeing short bursts from projectless API keys that push a tenant into the next rateband and trigger alerts. Thinking about a smoothing heuristic for service identity routing to avoid noisy ownership flips.

maria: yup, saw that in last night's spike. The console shows multiple projects as owners for minutes which is confusing.

kevin: can you sketch what you mean by smoothing? sticky routing window? fallback limits?

alex: idea: keep a short sticky affinity for a key -> project mapping (say 15m sliding window) then decay to a default org bucket. For projectless keys, route to org-default but allow temporary elevation to project band if sustained QPS > threshold for N seconds.

maria: sounds reasonable. how do we avoid gaming / DoS where bursts keep resetting the sticky window?

alex: add a cool-down: after a demotion back to org-default, require a higher sustained threshold or longer window to elevate again for that key; also cap consecutive elevations to 3 in a rolling 24h.

kevin: telemetry wise we need to record the decision and the signal that caused it — origin key id + routed_band + reason (sustained|burst|manual). otherwise we won't be able to explain alerts.

jess: agree. plus console should show the current affinity and recent transitions. not just the final owner. ops folks kept asking "who moved my traffic" during the spike.

alex: exactly. proposal: add tags to existing request span: routing.affinity_owner, routing.affinity_ttl_sec, routing.decision_reason. sample: `routing:{owner:project:foo,reason:sustained,ttl:900}`. store as string field in trace and 1% sample in request logs for full context.

kevin: what about quotas? if we elevate a key into project band temporarily, do we debit project quota or org-default?

alex: debit whichever band we actually route into. But put a shadow/debit counter to the origin org bucket to surface anomalies — if project gets elevated a lot, org quota might starve.

maria: we should also add a per-key SLO violation counter so alerts fire on sustained routing-induced breach instead of single-hit.

kevin: rollout plan? need to be cautious with billing and quotas.

alex: rollout idea: feature flag behind canary for 5% of keys, metric set: transitions/sec, avg affinity_ttl, #elevations per key, project quota delta. Run for 48h then expand.

jess: add a read-only console panel for the canary keys showing transition timeline (one-line per key) — ops can eyeball before full expansion.

maria: what about UI changes: display "Active routing" under key detail with a tooltip that explains the sticky heuristic and how to pin/override. Also an override API to pin a key to a band with 1h/24h/permanent options.

kevin: API design: POST /keys/:id/route-override {band: "project:foo", ttl_sec: 3600, reason: "support"} — returns previous affinity. Need audit log entry + rate limit.

alex: good. for safety, require admin scope to set override and surface in console audit trail.

ops-bot: Deploy canary flag to staging completed at 1718812380 :rocket:

maria: staging looks clean. one odd thing: for a few keys the affinity_ttl shows 0 immediately after elevation. might be a race in the cache set path.

kevin: send me the key ids, I'll check the cache write path. might be TTL unit mismatch (ms vs sec).

alex: reproduced locally — the commit I pushed used ms. fixing and will roll patch to staging.

jess: once patched, let's run a synthetic burst test: 2k rps for 60s then drop. watch transitions and alerts.

ops-bot: Canary patch rolled to staging at 1718812405.

kevin: running synthetic now. will post results in 30m.

maria: one more ask — telemetry sample should include the console-visible "transition reason" string so support can search logs directly.

alex: ack. final config we want: affinity_window_sec=900, elevation_threshold_rps=10, sustain_window_sec=30, demotion_cooldown_sec=3600, max_consecutive_elevations=3, telemetry_sample_pct=1.

jess: sounds good. can we get a follow-up to add an analytics job to compute per-key elevation rates daily? would help with tuning.

alex: adding to backlog — will open a short RFC and link here.

kevin: RFC would be great. add a section on quota accounting and shadow debits.

maria: thanks team. feels like a safer model than current flip-flop behavior. :+1:

alex: I'll open the RFC + patch for the TTL bug fix.

ops-bot: Created ticket PLAT-7892: "Routing affinity smoothing RFC + patch" assigned to alex (link: https://tracker/redwood/PLAT-7892)

kevin: tidy thread. we'll reconvene after canary metrics.
